caption: What if you lived on the International Space Station for a day? Your home flies about 400 km up at nearly 28,000 km/h and circles Earth every 90 minutes, so you'd see about 16 sunrises and 16 sunsets a day. You'd float, but not because gravity is gone: up there it's still about 90% as strong as on the ground. You float because you and the station are falling around Earth together. Chai won't pour, it drifts in blobs, so astronauts sip drinks from pouches with straws. Your spine stretches too, and astronauts can grow up to 3% taller, about 5 cm, until they return home. The ISS recycles 98% of the crew's water, including sweat and urine. Diwali diyas? Flames are only lit inside special experiment racks, and in microgravity they burn round and blue. Plot twist: the viral 'India on Diwali from space' photo is really a 2003 map of city lights growing over time. Would YOU live on the ISS? 👇
